parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: the penal code criminalises same-sex conduct, and the dossier documents its use against trans people. A trans woman was sentenced to 8 years in a men's prison (2021) and an earlier trans woman to 14 years, pardoned after one year. Police arrest and detain trans people, and community police forcibly strip and examine arrestees. Medical services are denied on gender-expression grounds. Officials and party figures have voiced hostility, and the 2024 Constitutional Court upheld the provisions. Recourse is largely absent: the moratorium was annulled and the court deferred reform. The only protection identified is a media-specific hate-speech rule with no documented enforcement. Border treatment of trans visitors is not documented, and no death penalty is documented. Rated at the Severe/High boundary, well above lethal-custody cases and below the 0.25 band only because no capital exposure or visitor-specific border rule is evidenced.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry, visa or passport-marker rules or border screening practice for trans travellers are documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document mismatch encountered at entry is unresolved; if it prompts a same-sex-conduct inquiry, it could feed into the custody pathway below.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police arbitrarily arrest and detain trans people and sometimes assault them. Arrests continued despite the moratorium, with charges shifted to section 156 to evade it. Arrestees face forced stripping, forced medical and HIV/STD examinations, extortion and photo distribution. Bail was denied to a trans woman on public-anger grounds.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The 2012–2016 moratorium was annulled; no current arrest suspension is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest exposes the traveller to community-police abuse and, on conviction, to lengthy imprisonment under the penal code.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A convicted trans woman was held in a men's prison for eight years (2021). Prison conditions are described as harsh, and a 2010 sentence was served with hard labour before a pardon.
federal_state_facilities.protection: A single presidential pardon (2010) is the only documented relief.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Conviction for same-sex-conduct offences routes a trans traveller into birth-sex custody with the documented harms that follow.

care_services.exposure: Medical staff denied services on gender-expression grounds. A trans man was beaten and refused treatment. Nurses mocked people seeking HIV tests.
care_services.protection: Official engagement on HIV services exists in principle but is not documented as reaching trans people.
care_services.interaction: Denial of care for a visitor who is outed or read as gender-nonconforming is documented as a plausible outcome.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Senior officials have framed same-sex activity as un-national and threatened activists. Religious and party figures have called for killing gay people. The constitutional court upheld criminalisation and held that reform is for the legislature. Mass protests have been held against legalisation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A 2019 broadcasting provision on gender-identity hate speech exists, with no documented enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile state framing lowers the chance that police or courts will treat a complaint from a trans visitor as credible.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. The dossier gives no account of minors or guardians travelling with trans adults.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian's same-sex or gender-nonconforming relationship could fall under the same arrest and custody exposure as an adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Neighbours and community police assaulted and threatened arrested men, with threats of being burned alive. Public hostility toward visibility is documented, including a gay man's brief detention and a period in hiding.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; police response to violence against trans people is not shown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response can itself be the source of violence, so a trans victim cannot rely on police protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No broad anti-discrimination law covers sexual orientation or gender identity. Constitutional challenges failed, and the court left reform to a legislature that has not acted. Marriage law fixes gender at birth. Enforcement of the 2019 broadcasting provisions is undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A limited media-specific hate-speech rule exists on paper, with no documented operation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is largely unavailable, so an outed visitor has little route to reversal of arrest, custody or care denial.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar. Both involve immorality or same-sex statutes used against gender-nonconforming visitors, custody with assault risk, and denial of relief. This dossier documents a higher conviction and sentence record, but it lacks the documented border-detention pathway and the rating is slightly higher because no death penalty is documented.

Similar. Both document birth-sex custody, cross-dressing or same-sex arrests, and weak remedies. This dossier adds convictions of trans women with long sentences and documented official hostility, so it sits slightly lower, while the other anchor documents formal prohibition of execution.

Lower. The 0.35 anchor documents stops and detention that rarely escalate to imprisonment. This dossier documents imprisonment of trans women for years, custody sentences, and community violence, which are more severe.

parsed.synthesis: Criminal exposure under same-sex-conduct provisions is applied to gender-nonconforming people in practice, with documented arrests, long sentences, and men's-prison placement. Arrest triggers community violence and forced examinations, with little state protection. Medical denial and official hostility compound the exposure, and recourse has been closed by courts and the executive. Documented protections are either annulled or unenforced. Visitor-specific border and minor-related risks are undocumented and are not counted, but the documented resident pattern would apply to any visitor who is outed or read as same-sex-coupled.
